target_customer: Men buying custom-fit dress shirts online
problem: Ordering shirts online meant guessing sizes, and tailor measurements required an in-person visit or a tape measure.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer made-to-measure apparel, measured by phone camera
product_category: Custom clothing ecommerce with computer vision measurement

founders.name: Miles Penn
founders.background_notes: YC page https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mtailor lists him as Founder/CEO, Stanford 2012. Secondary sites name Rafi Witten as co-founder; not confirmed by a primary source so not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting accurate body measurements from phone camera images in 2014 needed computer vision and a made-to-measure supply chain.

defensibility.rationale: Measurement data and fit models could compound, but made-to-measure shirts were already sold online by others and the measuring method was reproducible.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition or copy was found; the company appears to still operate.

market_need_then: Launch coverage in 2014 (TechCrunch, Business Insider) positioned a 69 dollar custom-fit shirt measured by phone as replacing tape measures.

branding.brand_signature: Measure yourself with your phone in under a minute
branding.community_and_virality: Appeared on Shark Tank (aired 2015 per secondary sources, no deal) and in men's style press.

brand_strength.rationale: Modest press and one TV appearance; no evidence of a strong community or recognition.

outcome_analysis: MTailor is listed as still operating after more than a decade, with small disclosed funding including a Wefunder crowdfunding campaign and Khosla Ventures as a reported investor. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found, and scale or revenue is unknown, so it reads as a long-running niche apparel business rather than a venture outcome.
notes: Company website mtailor.com returned HTTP 403 when fetched. Funding sources conflict: aggregators give a 2M seed in 2014 led by Khosla Ventures, 5.2M Series A in 2018, totals from 2.1M to 7.2M, and CB Insights gives 4.15M including a 2.13M convertible note in September 2023. These are aggregators only and not recorded as rounds. The Wefunder figure is the platform's own total raised and the Wefunder campaign date was not read. No dated 2014 competitor source was found, so the list is empty.
